title.narrative: East Africa Integrated Community HIV and AIDS Programme

description.narrative:
Dar-es-Salaam Archdiocese Community Health Education Programme (DACHEP) and Pastoral Activities and Services for people with AIDS in Dar-es-Salaam Archdiocese (PASADA) {thus DACHEP/PASADA} have been in partnership with CAFOD since 2004. DACHEP/PASADA implemented the successful joint programme funded by Comic Relief (October 2004 – September 2007) to Strengthen community responses to HIV and AIDS in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. DACHEP/PASADA aimed to provide education on health and HIV and AIDS as well as offer comprehensive prevention, care, treatment and support services to people living with HIV and AIDS. Both organisations have an extensive community-based outreach network that directly impacts the daily lives of adults and children infected and affected by HIV and AIDS.
The current project titled ‘East Africa Integrated Community HIV and AIDS Programme' was intended to bring on board 4 partners from Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda namely DACHEP/PASADA, Integrated AIDS Programme, Nsambya Home Care Programme and Hospice Africa Uganda respectively. The Programme was aimed to provide learning opportunities as well as expand the project scope to reach more adults and children infected and affected by HIV and AIDS for all implementing organisations. This programme was successful to receive funding from Comic Relief for DACHEP/PASADA project only. Successful DP partnership has demonstrated results such as strengthened community capacity and behaviour change via Stepping Stones training. However, there is need to provide continued comprehensive prevention education through various channels of education as revealed DP evaluation and mid term review.
During this reporting period, DP continued to provide HIV and AIDS prevention education, community health education and offered referral support for PLWHA and OVCs through community volunteers. This activities increased access to voluntary counselling and testing services provided by DP and home based care support for PLWHA provided by PASADA. Awareness creation on the needs of PLWHA and OVC was conducted resulting in their greater acceptance and support by the community. The use of the Stepping Stones approach, a life skills and behaviour change tool will continue to increase education in the community and enable community members to know their HIV status and adopt positive approaches to life.
